records.label: F
records.text: 3 tbsp cumin, dark chocolate, a bay leaf.

steps.name: emit
steps.title: Write it down
steps.text: Rosa writes down Grandma's chili as a record of recipe:chili. It is checked, signed and added to the store. There is one record, so the recipe has one head: the version that nothing replaces.

steps.name: revise
steps.title: Change it
steps.text: Rosa wants more cumin. Her new record B names A in prev, so B replaces A. Nothing is edited in place. A is still in the store, replaced, and B is the head.

steps.name: fork
steps.title: Two at once
steps.text: Ben's phone holds only A, and he changes it too: he adds chocolate. Now two records replace A, so the recipe has two heads. That is a fork, and both are shown. C is listed first because it was written later. Which one arrived first never decides.

steps.name: merge
steps.title: Join them
steps.text: Rosa writes M, which names both B and C in prev: more cumin, and the chocolate. One head again. Joining is an ordinary write whose prev lists two records, not a verb of its own.

steps.name: erase
steps.title: Erase a mistake
steps.text: A had the cabin's door code in it by mistake. Rosa's next record, E, changes nothing in the recipe and erases A. A keeps its id, its signature and its place. Only what it said is gone, for everyone who holds E. The count still says five, because counting needs no payload.

steps.name: any-order
steps.title: Any order
steps.text: Deliver the same five records in any order, to any phone, and every answer comes out the same. The set decides, not the sequence. That is how late arrivals, copies sent twice and two-way syncs agree.

steps.name: less-in-view
steps.title: Less in view
steps.text: Kim's copy holds E without what it says. Kim still sees that E is the head, because prev is on the envelope and every reader holds envelopes. The answer says E's words are withheld instead of guessing. The count, which needs no payload, is still five.

steps.name: tick
steps.title: Freeze it
steps.text: For the printed family cookbook, the answer is frozen: a tick fixes the result together with the exact five records it read. Anyone who holds those five gets the same tick, so others can point to it.

steps.name: back-to-text
steps.title: Back to text
steps.text: A lens shows the head as a section of text. Ben adds a bay leaf. Parsing finds one accepted edit, and applying it writes F, which replaces E. The edit is a record again, and the loop closes.
